claims.text: The proposed material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
An NbMoCrTiAl high-entropy-alloy composite containing in-situ TiC and Al2O3 reinforcements can be produced through powder processing followed by SPS.
Rapid quenching immediately after SPS will refine eutectic lamellar spacing relative to conventional cooling.
Rapid quenching immediately after SPS will improve interfacial bonding relative to conventional cooling.
Rapid post-SPS quenching will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to conventionally cooled samples.
The intervention is an immediate post-SPS quench with a substantially higher cooling rate than standard processing.
The comparison should hold sintering conditions constant and vary only cooling rate.
The proposed structural mediator includes a more homogeneous dispersion of a continuous ductile matrix.
Accelerated cooling suppresses coarsening of the ductile matrix.
Accelerated cooling suppresses coarsening of brittle reinforcing phases.
Microstructural refinement creates stronger barriers to dislocation motion and thereby increases strength.
Improved interfacial continuity and smaller brittle phases delay crack initiation and propagation, thereby increasing ductility.
Quenched samples are expected to have higher yield strength than conventionally cooled SPS samples.
Quenched samples are expected to have higher strain to failure than conventionally cooled SPS samples.
Excessive quench-induced residual stress or processing defects could negate the mechanical benefits.
Departure from the eutectic composition or extreme cooling rates that induce phase instabilities could negate the improvements.

The hypothesis is falsified if quenching fails to refine the microstructure and fails to produce a statistically significant simultaneous increase in strength and ductility, or if quench-induced defects deteriorate mechanical performance.
